title: Buoy Work in the Rio Bravo Is Clogging Nuevo Laredo's Water Plant Intakes
excerpt: Sediment stirred up by boats placing buoys in the Rio Bravo is clogging the intakes of Nuevo Laredo's Norte and Centro water plants. COMAPA says no customers have lost service so far, but cleaning dives have jumped from twice a day to as many as ten.
content:
Sediment stirred up by boats placing buoys in the Rio Bravo is clogging the intake structures of Nuevo Laredo's Norte and Centro water treatment plants, according to Red Metropolitana.

Silvia Ariadna Fernández Gallardo, general manager of the city's water utility COMAPA, confirmed that both plants were affected this week, Red Metropolitana reported. The problem appeared first at the Norte plant and then at the Centro plant, where sediment is blocking the intakes and slowing the normal flow of water into the facilities.

So far, the obstructions have not affected service to customers, Fernández Gallardo said, but they mean extra work for operations staff, especially the divers who clear sediment and free the intake structures.

Under normal conditions, cleaning dives are done twice a day. With the obstructions, crews have had to increase dives to four, five or even ten times a day to restore normal intake capacity, according to Red Metropolitana.

Fernández Gallardo said COMAPA has already contacted the International Boundary and Water Commission, known in Mexico as CILA, through the proper channels to ask its U.S. counterpart to stop the maneuvers that are harming the plants. About five buoys still need to be recovered, and the utility is also in contact with local authorities about the situation.

The buoy work runs from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., according to Red Metropolitana. COMAPA is keeping up the extra cleaning work to make sure the obstructions do not compromise the intake and supply of drinking water in Nuevo Laredo.

The buoy placement in the river has already drawn scrutiny this week, and this is the latest development in the ongoing work on the Rio Bravo.

Source: Red Metropolitana, November 14, 2026.
